# PR #2600: Patch: the AI prices the Start of turn and End of turn effects of Units on the board, on both sides

Closes #2565

The AI now prices one firing of a Unit's Start of turn and End of turn effects, for Units on either field. An enemy Gatling Pea therefore counts as an engine instead of a 2/6 body, and an own Gravedigger counts for more than a blank body of its size. The two decision cases in the acceptance criteria already came out right before this change, so their tests are guards. The tests that fail without the change are the price and worth ones.

## What changed

- **Which cards are probed.** `turn_hook_prices` in `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs` now fires each hook for:
  - every unit on either field;
  - the seat's own backrow;
  - the enemy's backrow cards the seat can read (`readable_by`, so a face-down card is never probed, R185);
  - the Units and Field Spells in the seat's own hand, spawned into the sandbox first. A Unit goes through a new `spawn_hand_unit`, which I pulled out of `spawned_death_probe` so both probes share it.
- **Whose view.** Each hook is priced from its controller's view. The enemy's Pea is priced by what its hit gives the enemy, and a hook that harms its holder prices below zero.
- **Where the price lands.** `unit_worth` adds `AI_EVAL.turn_hook` times the price, so `kill_worth` and every other `unit_worth` caller carry it. `material` now adds it for a readable backrow card on either side, not just the seat's own.
- **Budget.** `AI_TURN_HOOK_PROBE_NODES` goes from 12 to 24, the same as the Death probes' cap. I did not measure it against 12; the gate's perf run is the only measurement.
- **Spec.** New ruling `R2565000` with its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/2565.md`. It edits `R2477000`'s "What is not priced" and "Rejected" lines and the §9.9 evaluation paragraph. The `crates/ai` README and the `config.rs` and `decide.rs` comments are updated to match.

## Tests

New `r2565000_*` tests in `crates/ai/tests/ai/turn_hooks.rs`:
- A Unit with a hook is priced on either field, and a duplicate card is probed once.
- `unit_worth` and `kill_worth` carry exactly `turn_hook × price`; the frozen baseline reads none.
- An enemy engine lowers the evaluation and an own one raises it.
- An enemy face-up Mana Well is priced; a face-down Ace in the Hole is not, and costs no node.
- Hand Units are priced by spawning first (2 nodes), including on a full row.
- A hand Unit without a hook is not probed.
- Meltdown Layer, whose hook harms it, prices below zero on both sides.
- A Gravedigger is priced by the card it returns.
- A crowded board on both sides stays within the 24-node cap and the decision budget.
- Acceptance 1: with one Hit Job, the AI removes the Gatling Pea over a 3/7 vanilla.
- Acceptance 2: the AI attacks with the vanilla, not its own Gravedigger, into an enemy Taunt 5/4, in either field order.

I changed the existing `r2477000_an_enemy_face_down_card_is_priced_as_before` to drop the enemy Mana Well, since an enemy face-up Field Spell is now priced.

The removal and trade tests pass with and without the new `unit_worth` term. I switched the term off and re-ran them, and scanned vanilla stats from 3/4 to 8/9 against the Pea. The decision flips at the same cells either way, because the AI's reply already plays out the enemy's end of turn and the seat's own start of turn. What the AI did not see before is the second and later firings and the Pea's growth.

## Results

- `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`: 26, 684 and 97 passed (7 ignored daily).
- `cargo test --workspace --features jackioh-engine/testkit,jackioh-engine/ts`: exit 0, and `apps/web/src/wire` has no diff.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo jackioh spec check`: "1562 rulings, 3634 proofs, 48416 citations in 3017 files, 19377 links: ok". `catalog check` and `patches check` are ok, and `classify --base origin/main --claims` says `Internal`.
- `cargo jackioh gate` (smoke):

  | Matchup | Wins | Needed |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | vs random | 19/20 | 17 |
  | vs greedy | 16/20 | 10 |
  | Hard vs Easy | 19/20 | 16 |

  There were no search panics, and the slowest scaled decision was 76 ms.
- Web: `apps/web/src/practice/claim.test.ts` passes without re-recording `practice-claim.json`, and all of `src/practice` passes (332 tests).
- Not run: workspace-wide clippy, `luau bench` (no parent-build comparison for decision time), 200 fuzz seeds, e2e, web typecheck and eslint. CI runs them.

## Decisions the issue did not settle

- **Dedupe.** A card is keyed by definition and face, so one price serves both sides. The seat's own board is probed first and sets it. I rejected probing each copy on its own, which costs a node for the same price.
- **Order.** Own board, then enemy board, then hand. This spends the budget on what a removal choice hinges on before the hand.
- **Weight.** `AI_EVAL.turn_hook` stays 0.5 and is not re-tuned. A single weight serves units and backrow cards; I rejected a separate unit weight.
- **Perspective.** Hooks are priced from the controller's view. I rejected pricing every hook from the seat's view, which would count the enemy's Mana Well mana as the seat's.
- **Departures from the plan:**
  - Hit Job costs 3, so that test gives the AI 3 mana.
  - The Gravedigger trade needs a forced trade, so the enemy is a Taunt body (Harmony Spirit, set to 5/4 through the scenario's stats override).
  - `R2565000`'s `cards` also lists R82, Core #6 and #16, and leaves out the Stinkyscape token.

## Look at twice

- `material` no longer limits the turn-hook term to the seat's own backrow. A readable enemy Field Spell with a hook now lowers the AI's evaluation, as intended.
- An animated backrow card that has both stats and a turn hook would have its hook counted twice, once in the backrow term and once in `animated_share × unit_worth`. No card in the current catalog has both, so I left it alone. I tried a fix and reverted it as unneeded.
- Enemy hooks are fired on the determinized probe world, so a hook that reads the enemy's hand is priced on a sample. That is the same exposure as the Death probes and not a leak: the probe world is built from the seat's view.

### Adversarial review

Approved on round 1 of 3.

Notes the reviewer left (not blocking):

- `crates/ai/tests/ai/turn_hooks.rs:498`: The two acceptance tests (the AI removes the Gatling Pea, and trades the vanilla before its Gravedigger) pass with or without the new `unit_worth` term, so they guard the behaviour but do not prove the change causes it.
- `crates/ai/src/config.rs:617`: `AI_TURN_HOOK_PROBE_NODES` went from 12 to 24 without being measured against 12, and no test fills the cap to show that probing stops when the budget runs out.
- `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:376`: Every caller of `unit_worth` now carries the hook price, including ones where the card cannot fire its hook: `dormant_worth`'s cards buried under the seat's own piles (R13: a buried card runs no hook) and `animated_share` in `material`, which can count a hook twice.
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/turn_hooks.rs:6`: The module header still says "the enemy's backrow is priced as before", which is no longer true for a readable enemy card.

# #2565: Patch: the AI prices the Start of turn and End of turn effects of Units on the board, on both sides
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
Some Units do something at the start or end of every turn. One grows and hits the enemy hero each turn; another hands its owner a card every turn. Since the last AI patch, the computer opponent counts this for its own backrow cards, but not for Units on the board, whether its own or the other player's. So it leaves a growing enemy engine alone to hit a plain body of the same size, and trades its own engines away as if they were blank. After this change, the AI counts one turn of such a Unit's effect on both sides of the board.

## Why
- R2477000's "What is not priced" list names "A unit's turn hooks" (`spec/rulings/R2477000.md:16`). It also leaves "probing the enemy's face-up Field Spells too, left for a later issue" (`:20`).
- `turn_hook_prices` keeps only backrow holders, `.filter(|holder| holder.zone == TriggerZone::Backrow)` (`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:1354`). The price is added only on the AI's own side, `if player == seat` (`evaluate.rs:724`).
- Real cards affected:
  - Gatling Pea (`crates/cards/src/scripts/meditative/c013_gatling_pea.rs`): "End of turn: Deal {damage} damage to the enemy hero. Then this damage permanently goes up by {growth}."
  - Gravedigger (`core/c037_gravedigger.rs`): "Start of turn: add a random card from your GY to your hand".
- `training/improve.md:100-101` names this as the loss the AI's training notes trace again and again: "an engine, a unit that grows or makes value every turn, priced at its body today and left unanswered".
- The learned weights (`crates/ai/src/learned/weights.json`, catalog v0.3.17) know none of the newer sets' cards, so the hand evaluation's price is the only one for them.

## Proposal
- Let `turn_hook_prices` probe field holders as well as backrow ones. Spawn hand Units into the sandbox first, as the Death probes do.
- Price the enemy's face-up holders from the enemy's view, on the enemy's own hook (its Start and End of turn).
- Add the `turn_hook` share of the price inside `unit_worth`, so a Unit's worth carries it wherever it is counted.
- Raise or split `AI_TURN_HOOK_PROBE_NODES` as measured.
- A new ruling in the issue's block amends R2477000's "What is not priced".

## Where it lands
`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`, `crates/ai/src/config.rs`, `crates/ai/tests/ai/turn_hooks.rs`, `crates/ai/README.md`, and `spec/rulings/R<n>.md` with its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/<issue>.md` (§9.9).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given one removal and two targets, an enemy Gatling Pea and an enemy vanilla Unit with equal or slightly better stats, the AI removes the Gatling Pea.
- [ ] With its own Gravedigger and a same-cost vanilla Unit on the board, the AI trades the vanilla first.
- [ ] Hidden cards are never probed (R185), and a hook that harms its holder prices below zero, as R2477000's do.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh gate` passes at smoke size, and the perf gate's decision time holds.

## Size and risks
Medium, and hard (AI). More probes per decision, bounded by the node constant. The Hard-vs-Easy gate must still pass, so the weight may need screening. Practice fixtures that pin the AI's moves may need re-recording.

## What it actually means
Some Units do something at the start or end of every turn. One grows and hits the enemy hero each turn; another hands its owner a card every turn. Since the last AI patch, the computer opponent counts this for its own backrow cards, but not for Units on the board, whether its own or the other player's. So it leaves a growing enemy engine alone to hit a plain body of the same size, and trades its own engines away as if they were blank. After this change, the AI counts one turn of such a Unit's effect on both sides of the board.

## Why
- R2477000's "What is not priced" list names "A unit's turn hooks" (`spec/rulings/R2477000.md:16`). It also leaves "probing the enemy's face-up Field Spells too, left for a later issue" (`:20`).

- `training/improve.md:100-101` names this as the loss the AI's training notes trace again and again: "an engine, a unit that grows or makes value every turn, priced at its body today and left unanswered".
- The learned weights (`crates/ai/src/learned/weights.json`, catalog v0.3.17) know none of the newer sets' cards, so the hand evaluation's price is the only one for them.

## Proposal
- Let `turn_hook_prices` probe field holders as well as backrow ones. Spawn hand Units into the sandbox first, as the Death probes do.
- Price the enemy's face-up holders from the enemy's view, on the enemy's own hook (its Start and End of turn).
